title: Soften the edges, keep the levels
story: A 5 V square wave (10 ms high, 10 ms low) drives a 10 uF capacitor through a resistor. You want soft edges: 1 ms after the wave jumps high the capacitor must still be at 3 V or less. But the signal must still reach its levels: at least 4.8 V just before the wave falls, and 0.2 V or less just before it rises again. Pick the resistor.

goals.label: soft edge: 3 V or less 1 ms after the rise
reaches at least 4.8 V before the fall
drops to 0.2 V or less before the next rise

hints: Charging: v = 5 x (1 - e^(-t / RC)). Discharging: v = V0 x e^(-t / RC).
Reaching 4.8 V of 5 V means the missing part is 4%: e^(-9.9 ms / RC) must be 0.04 or less.
Being at 3 V or less after 1 ms means e^(-1 ms / RC) must be 0.4 or more. Turn both into limits on RC, then divide by 10 uF.
